findings.en_sentence: Brachiosaurus fossils were first found in the Colorado River valley in western Colorado, United States.
findings.es_sentence: Los fósiles de Brachiosaurus se encontraron por primera vez en el valle del río Colorado, en el oeste de Colorado, Estados Unidos.
findings.problem: Says Brachiosaurus fossils were 'first found' in the Colorado River valley, but sentence 9 says a Brachiosaurus skull was found in 1883 at Garden Park (and the holotype was only dug up in 1900); the source only says Riggs described it from fossils found there.
findings.correct: The genus was described in 1903 from fossils (the holotype) found in the Colorado River valley of western Colorado.
findings.checked_in: enwiki intro + Holotype specimen; F003, F015

findings.en_sentence: A Brachiosaurus skull was discovered in 1883 by farmer Marshall Parker Felch near Garden Park, Colorado.
findings.es_sentence: Un cráneo de Brachiosaurus fue descubierto en 1883 por el granjero Marshall Parker Felch cerca de Garden Park, Colorado.
findings.problem: Felch reported 'a sauropod skull' in 1883; it was long taken for a Camarasaurus-type skull and was only assigned to Brachiosaurus sp. in 1998 (Carpenter & Tidwell). As written, it reads as a skull recognized as Brachiosaurus in 1883.
findings.correct: In 1883 Felch found a sauropod skull near Garden Park, Colorado, which was assigned to Brachiosaurus in 1998.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Assigned material (Felch Quarry skull, McIntosh & Berman 1975, Carpenter & Tidwell 1998); F015

findings.en_sentence: A 1997 study by Leonardo Salgado suggested that Brachiosaurus and related genera were not a separate branch but offshoots of the Titanosauriformes stem group.
findings.es_sentence: Un estudio de 1997 de Leonardo Salgado sugirió que Brachiosaurus y los géneros relacionados no formaban una rama separada, sino que eran ramificaciones del grupo troncal de los Titanosauriformes.
findings.problem: Salgado et al. (1997) put brachiosaurids as successive offshoots of the stem *within* Titanosauriformes (a clade they named and that includes Brachiosaurus). 'Offshoots of the Titanosauriformes stem group' / 'grupo troncal' implies they fall outside Titanosauriformes.
findings.correct: ...suggested that brachiosaurids were not a natural group of their own but successive offshoots along the lineage within Titanosauriformes.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Classification; F058; knowledge (Salgado, Coria & Calvo 1997)

findings.en_sentence: In 2016, Hallett and Wedel rejected the hypothesis that Brachiosaurus nostrils were at the snout tip, suggesting they were placed at the top of the head as traditionally thought.
findings.es_sentence: En 2016, Hallett y Wedel rechazaron la hipótesis de que las fosas nasales de Brachiosaurus estuvieran en la punta del hocico, sugiriendo que estaban situadas en la parte superior de la cabeza como se pensaba tradicionalmente.
findings.problem: Rejects a 'snout tip' hypothesis that the page has not introduced yet; whose hypothesis it was (Witmer 2001) only appears in the next sentence, so the two read as unrelated and out of order.
findings.correct: Put Witmer's 2001 hypothesis first, then: in 2016 Hallett and Wedel rejected Witmer's idea and placed the nostrils at the top of the head, as traditionally thought.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Nostrils (paragraphs on Witmer 2001 and Hallett & Wedel 2016); F071, F072

findings.en_sentence: Large-scale expeditions in German East Africa discovered significant brachiosaurid fossils in the Tendaguru Formation between 1909 and 1912.
findings.es_sentence: Expediciones a gran escala en el África Oriental Alemana descubrieron importantes fósiles de braquiosáuridos en la Formación Tendaguru entre 1909 y 1912.
findings.problem: In the Brachiosaurus discovery section, the Tendaguru finds read as Brachiosaurus material, but the page never says they are now Giraffatitan (sentence 18 assumes the reader already knows).
findings.correct: Add that this African material was first named Brachiosaurus brancai and is now the separate genus Giraffatitan.
findings.checked_in: enwiki Brachiosaurus brancai and B. fraasi; F023, F028

findings.es_sentence: Czerkas especuló que la gran abertura nasal de Brachiosaurus podría haber alojado tejido para un olfato mejorado, señalando que la ubicación exacta de las fosas nasales sigue siendo inconclusa sin impresiones de piel.
findings.correct: ...la ubicación exacta de las fosas nasales no puede determinarse con certeza sin impresiones de piel.

findings.es_sentence: En 1990, Stephen Czerkas hipotetizó que Brachiosaurus entraba ocasionalmente en el agua para regular su temperatura corporal.
findings.problem: 'Hipotetizó' is an anglicism not in the DLE.
findings.correct: En 1990, Stephen Czerkas planteó que Brachiosaurus entraba ocasionalmente en el agua...

findings.es_sentence: Existe un debate sobre la longitud del cuello, con Gregory S. Paul sugiriendo en 1988 que era más corto que el de Giraffatitan, mientras que Mike P. Taylor argumentó en 2009 que las proporciones de las vértebras indicaban lo contrario.
findings.problem: 'con Gregory S. Paul sugiriendo...' is an English 'with + -ing' construction.
findings.correct: Existe un debate sobre la longitud del cuello: Gregory S. Paul propuso en 1988 que era más corto que el de Giraffatitan, mientras que Mike P. Taylor argumentó en 2009...

findings.es_sentence: El nombre Giraffatitan fue elevado al estatus de género completo por George Olshevsky en 1991 basándose en diferencias en la variación vertebral.
findings.problem: 'Elevado al estatus de género completo' is a calque of 'full genus status'.
findings.correct: Giraffatitan fue elevado a la categoría de género por George Olshevsky en 1991...
